title: Accountability for all processing including processors
legalReference: DPDP Act s.8(1)
description: The Data Fiduciary is responsible for compliance for all processing undertaken by it or on its behalf by a Data Processor, irrespective of any agreement to the contrary.
question: Has the organisation formally assigned ownership of DPDP compliance (with board/management visibility) covering processing done by its processors?
guidance: Name a single accountable owner with board visibility. Document roles of DPO/privacy officer, IT security, HR, legal and business owners. Record that processor activity is in scope.
evidenceRequired: Board/management resolution or appointment letter; RACI matrix; compliance charter
penaltyReference: Schedule item 7 - up to Rs 50 crore (residual)

title: Technical and organisational measures for effective observance
legalReference: DPDP Act s.8(4), DPDP Rules Rule 6(1)(g)
description: Implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure effective observance of the Act and Rules.
question: Are documented policies, procedures, training and periodic reviews in place to operationalise DPDP obligations?
guidance: Maintain a DPDP policy framework (prefer amending existing HR, IT security, vendor and retention policies over creating new stacks), train staff, and review at least annually.
evidenceRequired: Approved data protection policy; training records; internal review reports
penaltyReference: Schedule item 7 - up to Rs 50 crore (residual)

title: Lawful purpose and permitted ground recorded for every processing activity
legalReference: DPDP Act s.4
description: Personal data may be processed only for a lawful purpose, on the basis of consent or a legitimate use under section 7.
question: Does every processing activity in the data inventory record its lawful purpose and its ground (consent or the specific s.7 legitimate use)?
guidance: Use the Data Inventory module to tag each activity with consent or the applicable s.7 clause (e.g. s.7(i) employment, s.7(a) voluntarily provided data).
evidenceRequired: Personal data inventory / record of processing with ground per activity
penaltyReference: Schedule item 7 - up to Rs 50 crore (residual)

title: Personal data inventory and data map maintained
legalReference: DPDP Act s.8(1), s.8(4), s.11
description: A current map of what personal data is held, why, where, who accesses it and which processors receive it is the foundation for notices, rights responses and safeguards.
question: Is there a current personal data inventory and data-flow map covering systems, locations, recipients and processors?
guidance: Populate the Data Inventory and Data Flow registers; review at least every 6 months or on system change.
evidenceRequired: Data inventory export; data flow diagrams; review sign-off
penaltyReference: Schedule item 7 - up to Rs 50 crore (residual)

title: Legitimate use under s.7(i) documented for employee data
legalReference: DPDP Act s.7(i)
description: Processing for the purposes of employment, or safeguarding the employer from loss or liability, is a recognised legitimate use and does not require consent.
question: Where employee data is processed without consent, is reliance on s.7(i) documented and limited to employment-related purposes?
guidance: Record s.7(i) as the ground for HR activities in the inventory; add a DPDP clause to existing HR policies rather than creating a separate HR privacy stack.
evidenceRequired: HR policy DPDP clause; inventory entries for HR processing
penaltyReference: Schedule item 7 - up to Rs 50 crore (residual)

title: Data accuracy where data drives decisions or is disclosed
legalReference: DPDP Act s.8(3)
description: Where personal data is likely to be used for a decision affecting the Data Principal or disclosed to another Data Fiduciary, ensure completeness, accuracy and consistency.
question: Are data quality controls in place for personal data used in decisions or shared with other Data Fiduciaries?
guidance: Identify decision-making and disclosure flows; implement validation, reconciliation and correction procedures.
evidenceRequired: Data quality procedure; validation rules; correction logs
penaltyReference: Schedule item 7 - up to Rs 50 crore (residual)

title: Notice accompanies or precedes every consent request
legalReference: DPDP Act s.5(1), DPDP Rules Rule 3
description: Every request for consent must be accompanied or preceded by a notice stating the personal data and purpose, how to withdraw consent and exercise rights, and how to complain to the Board.
question: Is a DPDP notice presented before or with every consent request (web, app, forms, call-centre, offline)?
guidance: Inventory all collection points. Ensure the notice is shown before the consent action and is retained with the consent record.
evidenceRequired: Screenshots of collection points; notice text; consent capture logs
penaltyReference: Schedule item 7 - up to Rs 50 crore (residual)

title: Notice is standalone, clear and itemised
legalReference: DPDP Act s.5(1), DPDP Rules Rule 3(a),(b)
description: The notice must be understandable independently of other information and give, in clear and plain language, an itemised description of personal data and the specified purposes with the goods, services or uses enabled.
question: Is the notice standalone and does it itemise each personal data element and each specific purpose?
guidance: Avoid referring the user to a long privacy policy; list data items and purposes in a short notice.
evidenceRequired: Notice text with itemised data/purpose table
penaltyReference: Schedule item 7 - up to Rs 50 crore (residual)

title: Notice gives links/means to withdraw, exercise rights and complain to the Board
legalReference: DPDP Act s.5(1)(ii),(iii), DPDP Rules Rule 3(c)
description: The notice must give the communication link to the website/app and other means to withdraw consent (as easily as it was given), exercise rights and make a complaint to the Board.
question: Does the notice include a direct link and other means to withdraw consent, exercise rights and complain to the Data Protection Board?
guidance: Include the rights/withdrawal URL, grievance contact and Board complaint route in every notice.
evidenceRequired: Notice text; working withdrawal link screenshot
penaltyReference: Schedule item 7 - up to Rs 50 crore (residual)

title: Notice available in English or Eighth Schedule languages
legalReference: DPDP Act s.5(3), s.6(3)
description: The Data Principal must have the option to access the notice and consent request in English or any language in the Eighth Schedule to the Constitution.
question: Can Data Principals access notices and consent requests in English or a relevant Eighth Schedule language?
guidance: Select languages based on customer base; record language versions in the Consent module.
evidenceRequired: Language versions of notice; language selector screenshot
penaltyReference: Schedule item 7 - up to Rs 50 crore (residual)

title: Notice to Data Principals whose consent pre-dates the Act
legalReference: DPDP Act s.5(2), DPDP Rules Rule 3
description: Where consent was given before commencement, give notice as soon as reasonably practicable describing the data, purpose, rights and complaint route.
question: Has a plan been made to send notices to existing customers/users whose consent was obtained before commencement?
guidance: Plan an email/in-app campaign; record delivery evidence.
evidenceRequired: Legacy notice campaign plan; delivery logs
penaltyReference: Schedule item 7 - up to Rs 50 crore (residual)

title: Consent is free, specific, informed, unconditional and unambiguous
legalReference: DPDP Act s.6(1)
description: Consent must be given by clear affirmative action, for a specified purpose and limited to data necessary for that purpose.
question: Is consent captured by a clear affirmative action, purpose by purpose, without pre-ticked boxes or bundling unnecessary data?
guidance: Separate purposes; remove pre-ticked boxes; do not condition service on consent to unnecessary data.
evidenceRequired: Consent UI screenshots; consent purpose list
penaltyReference: Schedule item 7 - up to Rs 50 crore (residual)

title: No consent clauses that infringe the Act
legalReference: DPDP Act s.6(2)
description: Any part of consent that infringes the Act (e.g. waiver of right to complain to the Board) is invalid.
question: Have terms and consent texts been reviewed to remove waivers or clauses that infringe the Act or other law?
guidance: Legal review of T&Cs, forms and consent text.
penaltyReference: Schedule item 7 - up to Rs 50 crore (residual)

title: Consent request includes DPO / authorised person contact
legalReference: DPDP Act s.6(3), DPDP Rules Rule 9
description: Each consent request must be in clear and plain language and give contact details of the DPO (where applicable) or an authorised person.
question: Does each consent request show the DPO or authorised contact person?
guidance: Add the privacy contact block to all consent requests.
penaltyReference: Schedule item 7 - up to Rs 50 crore (residual)

title: Withdrawal as easy as giving consent
legalReference: DPDP Act s.6(4), DPDP Rules Rule 3(c)(i)
description: Where consent is the basis, the Data Principal may withdraw at any time with ease comparable to giving consent.
question: Can a Data Principal withdraw consent through the same channel and with comparable effort as it was given?
guidance: Provide one-click withdrawal in account settings / unsubscribe links; record withdrawals in the Consent module.
penaltyReference: Schedule item 7 - up to Rs 50 crore (residual)

title: Processing ceases (including at processors) after withdrawal
legalReference: DPDP Act s.6(6), s.8(7)
description: After withdrawal, cease and cause Data Processors to cease processing within a reasonable time unless required or authorised by law.
question: Is there a process that propagates consent withdrawal to all internal systems and processors within a defined time?
guidance: Define an SLA; automate propagation via API/webhooks; confirm with processors.
penaltyReference: Schedule item 7 - up to Rs 50 crore (residual)

title: Ability to prove notice and consent
legalReference: DPDP Act s.6(10)
description: In any proceeding, the Data Fiduciary must prove that notice was given and consent was obtained in accordance with the Act and Rules.
question: Are consent records (notice version, timestamp, purpose, channel, identifier) retained in a tamper-evident form?
guidance: Use the Consent module or API to log every consent event with notice version and timestamp.
penaltyReference: Schedule item 7 - up to Rs 50 crore (residual)

title: Consent Manager integration (if used)
legalReference: DPDP Act s.6(7)-(9), DPDP Rules Rule 4, First Schedule
description: Data Principals may give, manage, review or withdraw consent through a Consent Manager registered with the Board.
question: If consent is accepted via Consent Managers, is the integration with a Board-registered Consent Manager in place and are its artefacts recorded?
guidance: Verify registration on the Board's website; record Consent Manager ID with each consent.
penaltyReference: Schedule item 7 - up to Rs 50 crore (residual)

title: Verifiable parental consent before processing child data
legalReference: DPDP Act s.9(1), DPDP Rules Rule 10
description: Obtain verifiable consent of the parent before processing any personal data of a child, with due diligence that the parent is an identifiable adult (using reliable identity/age details held, or voluntarily provided details or a virtual token, e.g. via DigiLocker).
question: Is there a mechanism to identify children and obtain verifiable parental consent with due diligence on the parent's adult identity?
guidance: Implement age-gating; verify parent via existing reliable data or a virtual token from an authorised entity.
penaltyReference: Schedule item 3 - up to Rs 200 crore (s.9)

title: No detrimental processing of children's data
legalReference: DPDP Act s.9(2)
description: Do not undertake processing likely to cause any detrimental effect on the well-being of a child.
question: Has processing of children's data been assessed for detrimental effect on well-being?
guidance: Document an assessment per child-related processing activity.
penaltyReference: Schedule item 3 - up to Rs 200 crore (s.9)

title: No tracking, behavioural monitoring or targeted ads to children
legalReference: DPDP Act s.9(3), DPDP Rules Rule 12, Fourth Schedule
description: Do not track, behaviourally monitor or target advertising at children, unless an exemption in the Fourth Schedule applies (e.g. educational institutions, healthcare, child-care, specified purposes).
question: Are tracking, profiling and targeted advertising disabled for children, or is a Fourth Schedule exemption documented?
guidance: Document any exemption relied upon and its conditions.
penaltyReference: Schedule item 3 - up to Rs 200 crore (s.9)

title: Verifiable consent from lawful guardian of person with disability
legalReference: DPDP Act s.9(1), DPDP Rules Rule 11
description: Verify that a guardian is appointed by a court, designated authority or local level committee under applicable guardianship law.
question: Is guardian appointment verified before accepting consent on behalf of a person with disability?
guidance: Collect and verify guardianship orders/certificates.
penaltyReference: Schedule item 3 - up to Rs 200 crore (s.9)

title: Erasure when consent withdrawn or purpose no longer served
legalReference: DPDP Act s.8(7)(a)
description: Unless retention is necessary for compliance with law, erase personal data on withdrawal of consent or as soon as it is reasonable to assume the specified purpose is no longer served.
question: Is there a retention schedule with defined triggers and erasure methods for each data category?
guidance: Define retention per inventory entry; schedule erasure jobs; keep legal-hold exceptions documented.
penaltyReference: Schedule item 7 - up to Rs 50 crore (residual)

title: Processors caused to erase data
legalReference: DPDP Act s.8(7)(b)
description: Cause Data Processors to erase personal data made available to them.
question: Do processor contracts and procedures require erasure (with confirmation) at end of purpose or on instruction?
guidance: Add erasure clauses and obtain certificates of deletion.
penaltyReference: Schedule item 7 - up to Rs 50 crore (residual)

title: Third Schedule time-based erasure with 48-hour advance intimation
legalReference: DPDP Act s.8(8), DPDP Rules Rule 8(1),(2), Third Schedule
description: E-commerce entities (>= 2 crore users), online gaming intermediaries (>= 50 lakh users) and social media intermediaries (>= 2 crore users) must erase data 3 years after the Data Principal last approached them, informing her at least 48 hours before erasure.
question: If a Third Schedule class applies, are inactivity-based erasure and 48-hour prior intimation implemented?
guidance: Implement inactivity tracking; send pre-erasure notice at least 48 hours before.
evidenceRequired: Erasure job configuration; notice templates; logs
penaltyReference: Schedule item 7 - up to Rs 50 crore (residual)

title: Minimum one-year retention of processing logs and associated data
legalReference: DPDP Rules Rule 8(3), Seventh Schedule
description: Retain personal data, associated traffic data and logs of processing for at least one year from the date of processing for Seventh Schedule purposes, then erase unless other law requires.
question: Are processing logs and associated personal data retained for at least one year (including at processors) and then erased?
guidance: Align log retention settings in SIEM/log platforms and at processors to >= 1 year.
penaltyReference: Schedule item 7 - up to Rs 50 crore (residual)

title: Encryption, obfuscation, masking or tokenisation
legalReference: DPDP Act s.8(5), DPDP Rules Rule 6(1)(a)
description: Secure personal data through appropriate measures such as encryption, obfuscation, masking or virtual tokens.
question: Is personal data encrypted at rest and in transit, and masked/tokenised where full values are not needed?
guidance: Validate configuration (not just tool presence): database TDE/column encryption, TLS 1.2+, masking in non-production.
evidenceRequired: Encryption configuration evidence; TLS scan; masking rules
penaltyReference: Schedule item 1 - up to Rs 250 crore (s.8(5))

title: Access control to computer resources
legalReference: DPDP Act s.8(5), DPDP Rules Rule 6(1)(b)
description: Appropriate measures to control access to computer resources used by the Data Fiduciary and its processors.
question: Are role-based access, MFA, privileged access management and periodic access reviews in place for systems holding personal data?
guidance: Run quarterly access reviews; enforce MFA for admins and remote access.
evidenceRequired: Access review reports; MFA policy; PAM configuration
penaltyReference: Schedule item 1 - up to Rs 250 crore (s.8(5))

title: Logging, monitoring and review of access to personal data
legalReference: DPDP Act s.8(5), DPDP Rules Rule 6(1)(c)
description: Visibility on access to personal data through appropriate logs, monitoring and review to detect unauthorised access, investigate and remediate.
question: Are access logs for personal data systems centrally collected, monitored with alerting and reviewed?
guidance: Feed logs into a SIEM (e.g. Wazuh, Sentinel, Splunk); define use cases for personal data access anomalies.
evidenceRequired: SIEM use-case list; alert samples; review records
penaltyReference: Schedule item 1 - up to Rs 250 crore (s.8(5))

title: Continuity measures such as backups
legalReference: DPDP Act s.8(5), DPDP Rules Rule 6(1)(d)
description: Reasonable measures for continued processing if confidentiality, integrity or availability is compromised, such as data backups.
question: Are backups taken, protected, and restore-tested for systems holding personal data?
guidance: Document backup schedule and test restores at least twice a year.
penaltyReference: Schedule item 1 - up to Rs 250 crore (s.8(5))

title: Log and personal data retention for one year for investigation
legalReference: DPDP Act s.8(5), DPDP Rules Rule 6(1)(e)
description: Retain logs and personal data for one year to enable detection, investigation and remediation, unless other law requires otherwise.
question: Are security logs retained for at least one year?
guidance: Check SIEM/log storage retention; also consider CERT-In 180-day log requirement.
penaltyReference: Schedule item 1 - up to Rs 250 crore (s.8(5))

title: Security safeguard clauses in processor contracts
legalReference: DPDP Act s.8(2), s.8(5), DPDP Rules Rule 6(1)(f)
description: Contracts with Data Processors must include appropriate provisions for reasonable security safeguards.
question: Do all processor contracts include security safeguard obligations equivalent to Rule 6?
guidance: Use the Vendor module to track DPA status and safeguard clauses per processor.
penaltyReference: Schedule item 1 - up to Rs 250 crore (s.8(5))

title: Organisational measures for observance of safeguards
legalReference: DPDP Act s.8(5), DPDP Rules Rule 6(1)(g)
description: Appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure effective observance of security safeguards.
question: Are security policies, training, vulnerability and patch management, and periodic testing in place?
guidance: Map to the Security Safeguards module controls and validate each with configuration evidence.
evidenceRequired: Security policy; VA/PT reports; patch compliance
penaltyReference: Schedule item 1 - up to Rs 250 crore (s.8(5))

title: Breach intimation to affected Data Principals without delay
legalReference: DPDP Act s.8(6), DPDP Rules Rule 7(1)
description: On becoming aware of a breach, intimate each affected Data Principal without delay, through her user account or registered communication mode, with description, likely consequences, mitigation, safety measures she can take, and a contact person.
question: Is there a procedure and template to notify affected Data Principals without delay with all Rule 7(1) contents?
guidance: Pre-approve templates; define who approves and sends; record each intimation.
evidenceRequired: Breach procedure; notification templates; drill report
penaltyReference: Schedule item 2 - up to Rs 200 crore (s.8(6))

title: Initial intimation to the Data Protection Board without delay
legalReference: DPDP Act s.8(6), DPDP Rules Rule 7(2)(a)
description: Intimate the Board without delay with a description of the breach, its nature, extent, timing, location and likely impact.
question: Is there a defined process, owner and channel for the initial intimation to the Board?
guidance: Track the 'without delay' intimation in the Incident module from the time of awareness.
penaltyReference: Schedule item 2 - up to Rs 200 crore (s.8(6))

title: Detailed report to the Board within 72 hours
legalReference: DPDP Act s.8(6), DPDP Rules Rule 7(2)(b)
description: Within 72 hours of becoming aware (or longer period allowed by the Board on written request), furnish updated details, facts and reasons, mitigation, findings about the person who caused it, remedial measures and a report on intimations to Data Principals.
question: Can the organisation produce the detailed Rule 7(2)(b) report within 72 hours of awareness?
guidance: Run a timed mock breach drill; keep a 72-hour timeline with evidence.
penaltyReference: Schedule item 2 - up to Rs 200 crore (s.8(6))

title: Coordinated CERT-In and sectoral reporting
legalReference: DPDP Act s.8(6), DPDP Rules Rule 7
description: DPDP breach intimation is separate from CERT-In cyber incident reporting (CERT-In Directions, 28 April 2022 - 6 hours) and sectoral regulators (e.g. RBI, SEBI, IRDAI). Deadlines differ.
question: Does the incident procedure handle DPDP, CERT-In and sectoral reporting from one incident record with separate deadlines?
guidance: Configure each reporting obligation in the deadline engine; assign owners.
penaltyReference: Schedule item 7 - up to Rs 50 crore (residual)

title: Breach response playbook, roles and drills
legalReference: DPDP Act s.8(5), s.8(6), DPDP Rules Rule 6(1)(g), Rule 7
description: A breach playbook defining who decides, who reports and who informs Data Principals, tested by drills.
question: Is there a breach playbook with named roles, and has a drill been run in the last 12 months?
guidance: Keep it short (one page) and executable; record drill timings against 72 hours.
penaltyReference: Schedule item 2 - up to Rs 200 crore (s.8(6))

title: Publish means to exercise rights and identifiers required
legalReference: DPDP Act s.11-14, DPDP Rules Rule 14(1)
description: Prominently publish on the website/app the means for making rights requests and the identifiers needed to identify the Data Principal.
question: Are rights request channels and required identifiers published prominently on website/app?
guidance: Publish a rights page with a form/email and list identifiers (e.g. customer ID, email, mobile).
penaltyReference: Schedule item 7 - up to Rs 50 crore (residual)

title: Right to access information
legalReference: DPDP Act s.11, DPDP Rules Rule 14
description: Provide a summary of personal data processed and processing activities, identities of other Data Fiduciaries and Processors with whom shared, and other prescribed information.
question: Can the organisation compile a summary of a Data Principal's data, processing activities and recipients?
guidance: Use the inventory to locate data; maintain response templates.
penaltyReference: Schedule item 7 - up to Rs 50 crore (residual)

title: Right to correction, completion, updating and erasure
legalReference: DPDP Act s.12, DPDP Rules Rule 14
description: Correct, complete or update data on request; erase on request unless retention is necessary for the specified purpose or legal compliance.
question: Are correction and erasure requests handled with verification, propagation to processors and documented exceptions?
guidance: Track each request in the Rights module with closure evidence.
penaltyReference: Schedule item 7 - up to Rs 50 crore (residual)

title: Right to nominate
legalReference: DPDP Act s.14, DPDP Rules Rule 14(4)
description: Enable Data Principals to nominate one or more individuals to exercise rights in the event of death or incapacity.
question: Is there a means to record nominations and act on nominee requests?
guidance: Add nomination capture to account settings or a form.
penaltyReference: Schedule item 7 - up to Rs 50 crore (residual)

title: Request verification
legalReference: DPDP Act s.11-14, DPDP Rules Rule 14(2)
description: Verify the identity of the requester using the particulars required under the terms of service.
question: Are requesters verified proportionately before data is disclosed or changed?
guidance: Define verification levels per request type.
penaltyReference: Schedule item 7 - up to Rs 50 crore (residual)

title: Effective grievance redressal mechanism
legalReference: DPDP Act s.8(10), s.13, DPDP Rules Rule 14(3)
description: Establish an effective mechanism to redress grievances and publish the response period, which must not exceed 90 days.
question: Is a grievance mechanism in place with a published response period of not more than 90 days, and is it tracked?
guidance: Publish the period; track grievances in the Rights module with SLA monitoring.
penaltyReference: Schedule item 7 - up to Rs 50 crore (residual)

title: Publish business contact of DPO or authorised person
legalReference: DPDP Act s.8(9), DPDP Rules Rule 9
description: Prominently publish on website/app, and mention in every response to a rights communication, the contact information of the DPO or a person able to answer processing questions.
question: Is the privacy contact published on the website/app and included in every rights response?
guidance: Add to website footer, app settings and response templates.
penaltyReference: Schedule item 7 - up to Rs 50 crore (residual)

title: Processors engaged only under a valid contract
legalReference: DPDP Act s.8(2)
description: A Data Processor may be engaged to process personal data on the Fiduciary's behalf only under a valid contract.
question: Is there a valid contract/DPA in place for every processor handling personal data?
guidance: Maintain the vendor register with DPA status; close gaps before commencement.
penaltyReference: Schedule item 7 - up to Rs 50 crore (residual)

title: Processor due diligence and periodic review
legalReference: DPDP Act s.8(1), s.8(5), DPDP Rules Rule 6(1)(f)
description: The Fiduciary remains responsible for processor activity; assess processor safeguards before and during engagement.
question: Are processors risk-assessed before onboarding and periodically reviewed?
guidance: Use vendor risk questionnaires; review high-risk vendors annually.
penaltyReference: Schedule item 7 - up to Rs 50 crore (residual)

title: Breach notification obligations on processors
legalReference: DPDP Act s.8(6), DPDP Rules Rule 7
description: Processors must promptly inform the Fiduciary of breaches so the Fiduciary can meet Rule 7 timelines.
question: Do processor contracts require breach notification to the Fiduciary within a defined short period (e.g. 24 hours)?
guidance: Set a contractual notification window well inside 72 hours.
penaltyReference: Schedule item 2 - up to Rs 200 crore (s.8(6))

title: Sub-processor control and data location
legalReference: DPDP Act s.8(1), s.16
description: Know which sub-processors and locations are involved in processing.
question: Are sub-processors and storage locations known and approved for each processor?
guidance: Require prior approval/notice of sub-processors.
penaltyReference: Schedule item 7 - up to Rs 50 crore (residual)

title: Cross-border transfers comply with Government restrictions
legalReference: DPDP Act s.16, DPDP Rules Rule 15
description: Personal data may be transferred outside India subject to restrictions notified by the Central Government, and requirements specified by general or special order regarding making data available to foreign States or entities under their control.
question: Are all cross-border transfers identified, and checked against Government notifications/orders and stricter sectoral rules (e.g. RBI data localisation)?
guidance: Flag transfers in the inventory; monitor MeitY notifications.
penaltyReference: Schedule item 7 - up to Rs 50 crore (residual)

title: Appoint a Data Protection Officer based in India
legalReference: DPDP Act s.10(2)(a)
description: An SDF must appoint a DPO based in India, responsible to the Board of Directors, representing the SDF and acting as point of contact for grievances.
question: Has a DPO meeting s.10(2)(a) criteria been appointed?
guidance: Board resolution appointing DPO; publish contact.
penaltyReference: Schedule item 4 - up to Rs 150 crore (s.10)

title: Appoint an independent data auditor
legalReference: DPDP Act s.10(2)(b), DPDP Rules Rule 13(1)
description: Appoint an independent data auditor to evaluate compliance.
question: Has an independent data auditor been appointed?
guidance: Engage an independent auditor; define scope.
penaltyReference: Schedule item 4 - up to Rs 150 crore (s.10)

title: Annual DPIA and audit with report to the Board
legalReference: DPDP Act s.10(2)(c), DPDP Rules Rule 13(1),(2)
description: Once every 12 months, undertake a DPIA and audit, and furnish the Board a report of significant observations.
question: Is an annual DPIA and audit performed and the significant-observations report furnished to the Board?
guidance: Use the DPIA module; schedule annually from notification date.
evidenceRequired: DPIA reports; audit report; Board submission
penaltyReference: Schedule item 4 - up to Rs 150 crore (s.10)

title: Due diligence on algorithmic software
legalReference: DPDP Rules Rule 13(3)
description: Verify that technical measures including algorithmic software are not likely to pose a risk to Data Principal rights.
question: Is there due diligence on algorithms/AI used in processing personal data?
guidance: Maintain an algorithm register with risk assessments.
penaltyReference: Schedule item 4 - up to Rs 150 crore (s.10)

title: Data localisation for specified personal data
legalReference: DPDP Rules Rule 13(4)
description: Ensure personal data specified by the Central Government (and its traffic data) is not transferred outside India.
question: Are controls in place to keep Government-specified data categories and traffic data within India?
guidance: Monitor Government specification; enforce in architecture.
penaltyReference: Schedule item 4 - up to Rs 150 crore (s.10)

title: Processing for subsidies/benefits follows Second Schedule standards
legalReference: DPDP Act s.7(b), DPDP Rules Rule 5, Second Schedule
description: State and its instrumentalities processing for subsidy, benefit, service, certificate, licence or permit must follow Second Schedule standards.
question: Does processing under s.7(b) follow Second Schedule standards (lawful, purpose-limited, accuracy, retention, safeguards, accountability)?
guidance: Document compliance per scheme.
penaltyReference: Schedule item 7 - up to Rs 50 crore (residual)

title: Research, archiving or statistical exemption meets Second Schedule standards
legalReference: DPDP Act s.17(2)(b), DPDP Rules Rule 16, Second Schedule
description: Exemption for research, archiving or statistical purposes applies only if processing follows Second Schedule standards.
question: If relying on the research/statistics exemption, are Second Schedule standards documented and met?
guidance: Document standards per project.
penaltyReference: Schedule item 7 - up to Rs 50 crore (residual)
